ai.description: This 30–35 mm frog is brown with dark mottling and a pale vertebral stripe. It features a pointed snout, distinct skin folds on the back, and lacks toe webbing. It is endemic to the Western Ghats.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Minervarya manoharani* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous glandular fold running along the dorsolateral sides of its back.
ai.habitat: *Minervarya manoharani* inhabits the humid evergreen forests and riparian zones of the Western Ghats, typically found at mid-to-high altitudes in leaf litter near streams.
ai.behavior: Manoharan’s Burrowing Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging from its subterranean retreats at night to forage for small invertebrates in moist soil and leaf litter.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Minervarya manoharani* breeds during the monsoon, laying clutches of approximately 200–300 pigmented eggs in shallow, temporary rain pools.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Minervarya manoharani* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala, India, typically inhabiting mid-to-high elevation regions.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Minervarya manoharani* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, metallic chirps, typically heard from flooded agricultural fields or marshes.
